summary:
MarsPath is an interactive prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge.

Future human exploration of Mars requires planning routes that balance scientific objectives with crew safety. However, information about rover trajectories, geological samples, and atmospheric hazards is often studied separately.

Our project integrates documented sample-site locations from NASA's Perseverance mission in Jezero Crater with an A* path-planning algorithm. Users can select scientific destinations, calculate round-trip trajectories, and evaluate how hypothetical dust storms and expedition time constraints affect route selection.

MarsPath combines real scientific references with clearly identified simulated environmental conditions. Although it is not an operational navigation or life-support system, the prototype demonstrates how future software could support the planning of scientific expeditions while prioritizing the safe return of explorers.
details:
Project Overview

MarsPath is an interactive software prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map."

Our project addresses the need for intelligent route-planning tools that balance scientific exploration with astronaut safety during future human missions to Mars.

How It Works

MarsPath uses documented locations associated with NASA's Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater, including Roubion, Rochette, Brac, Issole, and Sid.

The software implements the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate candidate round-trip routes between selected scientific destinations. Users can modify hypothetical dust-storm scenarios, travel speed, research duration, and available expedition time.

The system evaluates estimated travel distance, activity duration, and remaining time margin, allowing users to explore how environmental conditions can affect route selection.

Technologies and Scientific Data

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI-assisted programming and documentation.

Scientific references include NASA Perseverance mission resources, documented Martian sampling locations, MEDA atmospheric observations, and published research on dust storms.

Innovation and Impact

Our proposal emphasizes the development of software that considers both scientific objectives and explorer survival when evaluating Martian trajectories.

Instead of simply visualizing previous rover routes, MarsPath introduces interactive route calculations and environmental risk scenarios to illustrate future expedition-planning decisions.

Limitations and Future Development

The current prototype uses simulated dust conditions, simplified terrain penalties, and estimated travel times. It does not provide real-time Martian weather forecasts or certified astronaut safety calculations.

Future development would incorporate validated terrain elevation models, atmospheric datasets, oxygen and energy constraints, and additional mission-planning parameters.

Our long-term objective is to support future scientific exploration of Mars through more informed route-planning decisions.

AI Assistance

OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-6) assisted with software development, route-planning code, technical writing, research organization, and presentation preparation. The team acknowledges this assistance and remains responsible for the submitted project.
